field_label: Select visa route: General Work Visa (s19) or Critical Skills Work Visa (s19A)
deadline_label: Before visa application is lodged; minimum 4 months before planned start date
non_obvious_official_guidance: The Immigration Act 13 of 2002 provides two principal routes for skilled foreign workers: the General Work Visa (s19(1)), which requires a certificate from the Director-General of Employment and Labour confirming no suitable South African citizen is available; and the Critical Skills Work Visa (s19A), which requires the occupation to appear on the gazetted Critical Skills List and carries no Labour Market Test requirement.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Employers routinely default to the General Work Visa without checking whether the role qualifies for the Critical Skills route. The Critical Skills route eliminates the Labour Market Test, removing 8–12 weeks from the pre-application timeline. The Critical Skills List is updated by Government Gazette notice; the latest gazetted version must be verified before choosing a route.
non_obvious_action_required: Download the current Critical Skills List from the DHA website and match the employee's formal occupation title and NQF qualification level against it. If the role qualifies, use the Critical Skills Work Visa route. Involve an accredited immigration practitioner to confirm the classification before committing to either route.
source: Department of Home Affairs — Immigration Act 13 of 2002, ss 19 and 19A

authority: Department of Home Affairs / Department of Higher Education and Training
field_label: Match employee occupation title and NQF level against current Critical Skills List
deadline_label: Before Critical Skills Visa application is lodged
non_obvious_official_guidance: The Critical Skills List specifies permitted occupations by standardised title and minimum NQF qualification level. Both the job title and the applicant's foreign qualification level (as evaluated by SAQA) must match the List entry exactly for the application to be accepted on the Critical Skills track.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Employment contract titles frequently differ from the standardised occupation titles on the Critical Skills List. For example, 'Software Developer' may appear on the List as 'Software and Applications Developer and Analyst'. A mismatch causes DHA to re-route the application to the General Work Visa track, requiring a Labour Market Test and adding weeks to the process.
non_obvious_action_required: Cross-reference the employee's contract title and duties against every Critical Skills List entry. Where the match is ambiguous, consult an immigration practitioner and obtain a formal written opinion before lodging. Retain documentary evidence of the occupation match on the visa application file.
source: Department of Home Affairs — Critical Skills List (Government Gazette)

field_label: SAQA evaluation of foreign educational qualifications
deadline_label: Initiate at least 6 months before planned arrival; SAQA processing takes 6–8 weeks after receipt of a complete file
non_obvious_official_guidance: Immigration Regulations require that all foreign academic qualifications submitted with a South African work visa application be evaluated by SAQA and assigned a South African NQF level. The SAQA evaluation certificate is a mandatory supporting document for both the General Work Visa and the Critical Skills Work Visa.
non_obvious_actual_reality: SAQA evaluations take 6–8 weeks from receipt of a complete file. Applications with missing or uncertified documents are returned and the processing clock restarts. Employees with qualifications from multiple institutions must submit certified documentation for each. Total elapsed time from initiating SAQA to receiving the certificate can reach 3–4 months. A visa application submitted to a South African mission without the SAQA certificate is rejected on the spot.
non_obvious_action_required: Initiate the SAQA evaluation as the very first step — before any other visa document preparation begins. Review the current document requirements on saqa.org.za. Provide certified copies of all transcripts, degree certificates, and identity documents. For Critical Skills applicants, confirm with the relevant professional statutory body whether a separate membership certificate is also required in addition to the SAQA evaluation.
source: South African Qualifications Authority — Foreign Qualifications Evaluation

field_label: Medical report on DHA form BI-811 completed by a DHA-designated practitioner
deadline_label: Complete within 6 months before visa application; certificate must still be valid on the date the visa is issued
non_obvious_official_guidance: Immigration Regulation 9(3) requires a medical report completed on DHA form BI-811 by a practitioner designated by the Director-General of Home Affairs for the country or region where the application is lodged.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The examining doctor must appear on the DHA designated practitioners list for the country of application — a company physician, specialist, or general practitioner not on the list is not acceptable regardless of qualifications. The sealed, signed envelope containing the completed BI-811 must be presented to the mission unopened; a tampered or re-sealed envelope is rejected. Some countries have very few designated practitioners, requiring travel to another city.
non_obvious_action_required: Obtain the current DHA designated practitioners list from the South African mission or consulate-general in the country of application. Book an appointment early. Confirm the practitioner still appears on the current list immediately before the appointment, as lists are updated. Deliver the sealed, unopened report envelope to the mission on the day of the visa appointment.
source: Department of Home Affairs — Immigration Regulations, Regulation 9(3) and Form BI-811

authority: Department of Home Affairs / Relevant national police authorities
field_label: Police Clearance Certificate from all countries of 12-month-plus residence in the past 10 years
deadline_label: Allow 60–90 days; certificates must be no older than 6 months at the date of visa application
non_obvious_official_guidance: Immigration Regulation 9(3)(c) requires a police clearance certificate from every country in which the visa applicant resided for 12 months or more during the 10 years immediately preceding the application — not merely the current country of residence.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Most applicants obtain clearance only from their current country, unaware that prior countries of long-term residence are also required. Omitting any required country causes outright rejection of the visa application. Processing times vary enormously: US FBI clearances take 6–12 weeks via a channeler; UK Disclosure and Barring Service takes 2–8 weeks; some countries have decentralised police systems requiring court records from each province of residence. Validity windows on clearances from some jurisdictions can expire before the visa is issued.
non_obvious_action_required: List every country where the employee lived for 12 or more cumulative months in the past 10 years and start clearance applications in all jurisdictions simultaneously. Where a country does not issue national police clearances, obtain notarised affidavits and an explanatory letter from that country's embassy, and confirm acceptability with the SA mission before submitting the application.
source: Department of Home Affairs — Immigration Regulations, Regulation 9(3)(c)

field_label: Department of Employment and Labour certificate — no suitable South African citizen available (General Work Visa only)
deadline_label: Begin 5–6 months before planned start date; the DEL process alone takes 8–12 weeks
non_obvious_official_guidance: Section 19(1) of the Immigration Act 13 of 2002 requires that a General Work Visa application be accompanied by a certificate from the Director-General of Employment and Labour confirming that, despite a diligent search, no suitable South African citizen or permanent resident with qualifications or skills and experience equivalent to those of the applicant was available.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The DEL scrutinises the genuineness of the Labour Market Test: advertisements must appear in media accessible to South African job-seekers, all SA applicants must be considered, and written reasons must justify why each was found unsuitable. Incomplete documentation or unconvincing rejection rationales lead to requests for supplementary information that can extend the process well beyond 12 weeks. The DEL certificate has a validity period; if it expires before the visa is issued or the employee arrives, the entire Labour Market Test must be repeated from the beginning.
non_obvious_action_required: Begin the DEL certification process as the first step in the General Work Visa timeline, months before the employee's intended start date. Retain comprehensive records of all job advertisements (dates, media, reach), all applications received, all interview notes, and written rationales for rejecting South African applicants. Confirm the validity period of the issued DEL certificate and ensure it will remain valid through the employee's actual entry into South Africa.
source: Department of Employment and Labour — Immigration Act 13 of 2002, s19(1)

step: Lodge visa application at SA mission
authority: Department of Home Affairs (via South African diplomatic mission)
field_label: Lodge work visa application at South African embassy, high commission, or consulate on form DHA-947
deadline_label: All supporting documents complete; lodge at minimum 60 days before planned travel
non_obvious_official_guidance: Work visa applications must be lodged in person at the South African diplomatic mission responsible for the applicant's country of habitual residence, with a complete set of prescribed supporting documents, on form DHA-947.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Many SA missions require appointment booking weeks to months in advance. Some missions outsource lodgement to Visa Facilitation Services (VFS Global) and will not accept direct walk-in applications. The application must be lodged at the mission responsible for the applicant's country of habitual residence — using a conveniently located mission in a third country is generally not permitted. Official processing times are stated as 10 business days but actual turnaround is commonly 4–12 weeks. Incomplete applications are returned without the right to supplement and without refund of application fees.
non_obvious_action_required: Confirm whether the SA mission in the applicant's country accepts direct applications or requires a VFS Global booking. Book the appointment as soon as the full document set is assembled. Prepare a document checklist against the mission's published requirements and verify every item before attending. Do not book any travel or accommodation in South Africa until the physical visa is in hand.
source: Department of Home Affairs — Visa Application Process and Form DHA-947

authority: Department of Home Affairs (Border Management Authority)
field_label: Verify passport endorsement and visa conditions at port of entry
deadline_label: On the day of first arrival in South Africa — before leaving the immigration desk
non_obvious_official_guidance: On entry to South Africa, the immigration officer endorses the passport with the visa reference and records specific conditions. For General Work Visa holders, the endorsement typically names the specific employer and states that the holder 'may not work for any employer other than [named employer]'.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The employer-specific condition is strictly enforceable: working for a subsidiary, an affiliate, or a client site under a secondment arrangement technically constitutes a status violation and can result in visa cancellation. The validity date stamped is an outer limit — the employee must depart or renew before that date, not on it. Errors in the endorsement (wrong employer name, wrong visa category) arefar easier to correct at the port of entry than after the officer has closed the file.
non_obvious_action_required: Before leaving the immigration desk, photograph the passport endorsement page. Verify that the employer name matches the employment contract, the visa category is correct, and the expiry date is as expected. If any discrepancy is found, raise it with the immigration officer immediately — do not leave the port of entry first.
source: Department of Home Affairs — Immigration Act 13 of 2002 and Border Management Authority Act 2 of 2020

authority: Department of Home Affairs / Relevant professional statutory body
field_label: Record 6-month deadline for professional statutory body registration (Critical Skills visa holders)
deadline_label: Within 6 months of first entry date; begin application in the first week
non_obvious_official_guidance: Immigration Regulations require Critical Skills Work Visa holders to register with the relevant professional or statutory body within six months of first entry into South Africa. This is a visa condition; failure to demonstrate compliance may jeopardise visa renewal.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Professional statutory bodies such as the Engineering Council of South Africa (ECSA), the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA), and the South African Institute of Chartered Accountants (SAICA) each have their own competency assessments, supervised practice periods, or examinations before granting full registration. A foreign professional may satisfy the DHA 6-month filing deadline yet not receive full body registration for another 6–12 months. What DHA requires is that the application be lodged and diligent progress demonstrated — the body's own processing time does not count against the visa holder, but the lodgement itself must be on time.
non_obvious_action_required: On the day of arrival, record the exact entry date and calculate the 6-month deadline. Within the first week, identify the correct professional statutory body for the employee's occupation — there may be more than one, and an immigration practitioner can confirm which body DHA will accept. Lodge the body registration application within the first month to allow processing time within the 6-month window.
source: Department of Home Affairs — Immigration Regulations (Critical Skills Work Visa conditions)

field_label: SARS income tax registration and individual tax reference number
deadline_label: Before first salary payment; in practice within the first two weeks of employment
non_obvious_official_guidance: The Income Tax Act 58 of 1962 requires every person earning income in South Africa — including foreign nationals on work visas — to register as a taxpayer with SARS and obtain an income tax reference number. Employers must obtain the employee's SA tax number to operate a compliant PAYE payroll.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Many foreign nationals believe they are exempt from South African income tax for the first 183 days because of a double tax agreement. Double tax treaty exemptions are not automatic: they must be actively applied for via a SARS tax directive, and SARS registration is a prerequisite regardless. An employer that runs payroll without the employee's SA tax number is in PAYE compliance breach, irrespective of whether a treaty exemption may ultimately apply.
non_obvious_action_required: Register on SARS eFiling immediately after arrival — or at a SARS branch — using the passport, valid work visa, and proof of South African address (a lease agreement, an employer letter confirming the SA work address, or a temporary hotel address for the interim period). Once registered, immediately assess whether a SARS PAYE directive should also be applied for.
source: South African Revenue Service — Individual Tax Registration (Income Tax Act 58 of 1962)

authority: Department of Employment and Labour — Unemployment Insurance Fund
field_label: Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) employer registration and employee enrollment
deadline_label: Employer must be UIF-registered before first salary payment; employee enrolled from first payroll
non_obvious_official_guidance: The Unemployment Insurance Act 63 of 2001 requires all employers in South Africa to register with the UIF and to deduct 1% of each employee's remuneration (up to the statutory earnings ceiling, reviewed annually by notice) as the employee's UIF contribution, with the employer contributing a matching 1%. Foreign nationals on work visas are covered by the UIF.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Employers frequently assume that foreign nationals on time-limited work visas are excluded from UIF. They are not, unless the employee's home country has a bilateral social security agreement with South Africa that specifically displaces UIF liability. South Africa's network of bilateral social security agreements is limited; the common case is that no agreement applies and full UIF contributions are due from the first payroll. Operating without UIF registration or contributions creates retrospective UIF liability, interest, and administrative penalties.
non_obvious_action_required: Confirm whether the employee's home country has a bilateral social security agreement with South Africa that covers UIF. If not — the common case — register the employer under UIF using form UI-8 if not already registered, and enrol the employee from the first payroll. Remit contributions and file the monthly EMP201 (SARS combined PAYE/SDL/UIF return) by the 7th of the following month.
source: Department of Employment and Labour — Unemployment Insurance Act 63 of 2001

step: SARS PAYE directive for DTA exemption
form_name: IRP3(a) or IRP3(b) — SARS eFiling directive application
field_label: Apply for SARS PAYE tax directive if a double tax agreement exemption may apply
deadline_label: Apply before first payroll run; SARS directive processing takes up to 21 business days
non_obvious_official_guidance: Where a double tax agreement (DTA) between South Africa and the employee's country of tax residence provides for an exemption or reduced rate on employment income (commonly Article 15 of OECD-model treaties), the employer must apply for a SARS tax directive before adjusting the PAYE withholding rate. The employer may not unilaterally apply the treaty exemption.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The most common error: the employer or employee self-certifies that the 183-day rule under the DTA is satisfied and withholds no PAYE. SARS does not recognise self-certification. Until SARS issues a formal directive, the employer must withhold PAYE at the marginal rate. Over-withheld amounts are recoverable in the employee's annual ITR12 return, but the employee suffers a cash-flow shortfall in the interim and the employer faces a potential PAYE assessment if a self-certified exemption is subsequently found invalid.
non_obvious_action_required: Assess whether the employee's home country has a DTA with South Africa and whether Article 15 conditions are met (days in SA, non-SA employer, no SA permanent establishment). If so, apply for a SARS PAYE directive via eFiling before the first payroll. Retain the issued directive on the payroll file for the duration of the assignment and review it at each payroll year-end.
source: South African Revenue Service — PAYE Tax Directives (Income Tax Act 58 of 1962)

authority: Relevant professional statutory body (e.g., ECSA, HPCSA, SACAP, SAICA)
field_label: Lodge professional statutory body registration application (Critical Skills visa holders)
deadline_label: Lodge within the first month to meet the 6-month DHA visa condition deadline
non_obvious_official_guidance: The relevant professional statutory body is determined by the employee's occupation: the Engineering Council of South Africa (ECSA) for engineers; the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) for health professionals; the South African Institute of Chartered Accountants (SAICA) for chartered accountants; the South African Council for the Architectural Profession (SACAP) for architects. DHA requires demonstrated registration or documented progress toward registration as a condition of the Critical Skills Work Visa.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Foreign professionals sometimes assume that existing home-country professional body membership satisfies the SA requirement. It does not. SA statutory body registration is a separate process. Some bodies require English-language academic transcripts with certified translations; others require competency assessments or bridging examinations for foreign-trained professionals that can take months to complete independently of the 6-month DHA deadline.
non_obvious_action_required: Identify the correct South African professional statutory body for the employee's specific occupation — there may be more than one, and the immigration practitioner or DHA can confirm which one satisfies the visa condition. Obtain the body's requirements for foreign-trained professionals and submit the application in the first month. Keep the body's acknowledgement of the application as documentary evidence for any future DHA compliance enquiry.
source: Department of Home Affairs — Immigration Regulations (Critical Skills Work Visa conditions)

authority: South African Revenue Service / Department of Employment and Labour — UIF
field_label: Monthly UIF contribution payment and EMP201 declaration
deadline_label: By the 7th of each month (or preceding business day) for the prior payroll month
source: Department of Employment and Labour — Unemployment Insurance Act 63 of 2001, s10; SARS EMP201

field_label: Monitor South African tax residence — physical presence test (91-day and 915-day thresholds)
deadline_label: Review at the end of each South African tax year (1 March – 28/29 February)
non_obvious_official_guidance: Under the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962, a natural person becomes a South African tax resident under the physical presence test if present in South Africa for: (a) more than 91 days in the current tax year; AND (b) more than 915 days in aggregate in the preceding five tax years, of which more than 305 days in each of any three of those years. A tax resident is liable to South African income tax on worldwide income from all sources.
non_obvious_actual_reality: An employee who crosses the physical presence threshold becomes taxable in South Africa on worldwide income — including employer pension contributions, share options vesting offshore, and income from foreign investments — from the date the threshold is breached, not from the following tax year. SARS does not notify the taxpayer when the threshold is crossed; it is entirely self-assessed. Tax residency also activates exit tax rules: if the employee later leaves South Africa and ceases to be a SA tax resident, they may be deemed to have disposed of all worldwide assets at market value on the cessation date.
non_obvious_action_required: Track the employee's South African presence days throughout the tax year using a dated day-count log. When the count approaches 80 days in a tax year, flag the approaching 91-day threshold to tax advisers. If residency will be triggered, model the worldwide taxation impact before year-end and brief the employee on the exit-tax implications if the assignment is time-limited.
source: South African Revenue Service — Income Tax Act 58 of 1962, definition of 'resident' in s1

field_label: Monitor employer Permanent Establishment (PE) risk in South Africa
deadline_label: Ongoing — review at assignment start, contract renewal, and any change in the employee's commercial authority
non_obvious_official_guidance: South Africa's double tax agreements (modelled on the OECD Model Convention) provide that a non-resident enterprise may create a taxable Permanent Establishment in South Africa through: (a) a fixed place of business; (b) a dependent agent who habitually concludes contracts on the enterprise's behalf in South Africa; or (c) a service PE, where the enterprise furnishes services in South Africa through the same or connected individuals for more than 183 days in any 12-month period.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Even where no physical office exists, a single senior employee with commercial authority to bind the foreign employer can trigger a dependent-agent PE. The service PE provision in many of South Africa's DTAs — including those with France, Germany, Norway, and the Netherlands — is activated when the same employee provides services in South Africa for more than 183 days in any 12-month window, a threshold entirely separate from the employee's personal income tax residence trigger. A PE creates South African corporate income tax obligations, potential transfer pricing exposure, and may require registration as an external company with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC).
non_obvious_action_required: Before the assignment commences, obtain a PE risk assessment from a South African corporate tax adviser covering all three PE categories under the applicable DTA. Structure the employee's contract-signing authority and commercial activities to mitigate dependent-agent PE risk. Track the employee's cumulative service days in South Africa against the service PE threshold in the applicable DTA. Repeat the review at each contract renewal and whenever the employee's role or commercial responsibilities change materially.
source: South African Revenue Service — International Tax and Double Tax Agreements

field_label: Annual SARS individual income tax return (ITR12)
deadline_label: Annual; eFiling deadline typically October–November following the tax year end (1 March – 28/29 February); SARS confirms the exact date each year
source: South African Revenue Service — Individual Income Tax Return ITR12

field_label: Radiological (chest X-ray) report from a DHA-designated radiologist
deadline_label: Complete within 6 months before visa application; must remain valid on the date the visa is issued
non_obvious_official_guidance: The chest X-ray / radiological report is required as part of the medical examination package under the Immigration Regulations, completed by a DHA-designated radiologist, and submitted as part of Form BI-811 alongside the general medical certificate.
non_obvious_actual_reality: DHA-designated radiologists are available only at a limited number of approved centres, which may be scarce or non-existent in the applicant's home country, requiring travel to the nearest approved facility. Critically, the 6-month validity runs from the date the X-ray is taken — not the date of visa application — so if visa processing is prolonged, the report can expire before a decision is issued, forcing a repeat examination at additional cost and delay. Applicants frequently attend a general radiologist or hospital radiology department unaware that non-DHA-designated results are rejected outright.
non_obvious_action_required: Verify the radiologist is on DHA's current approved list before booking (the list is updated periodically and approvals can lapse). Time the appointment to account for expected visa processing duration: if processing typically takes 4–8 weeks, schedule the X-ray no earlier than 4–5 months before intended travel to preserve validity buffer. Request and retain the original stamped radiological report — DHA requires the original, not a photocopy or scan. If applying from abroad, contact the nearest South African embassy or VFS Global centre to obtain the current approved-radiologist list for your country.
source: Department of Home Affairs — Immigration Regulations (GN R413 of 2014) and Form BI-811
